items.hypothesis: A self-improving system can minimise surprise by AVOIDING hard tasks (the dark-room problem, active inference / Friston) — high stability that is really degeneration. Detect it: tag eval cases with difficulty (1 toy / 2 realistic / 3 adversarial); a set with no case >=2 is a dark room (only convergence-prone easy cases -> can't reveal a skill's value, mirroring strata's own 'sonnet converges to 0% on easy traps' finding). Borrow: zone-of-proximal-development / easy-to-hard curricula (arxiv 2602.10014). Not novel — the honest gate is the point.
items.ship_test: dark-room.mjs flags a set with only difficulty-1 cases as a dark room; l0-ponytail (3 toy + 4 realistic) reads ok.
items.resolution: 2026-07-06: shipped — optional `difficulty` field on eval cases + scripts/dark-room.mjs (pure coverage + dark-room verdict, self-tested, in CI). l0-ponytail tagged as the worked example (ok: 4 discriminating); the other 6 sets honestly flagged untagged, accruing when touched. Gate-type; the time-series ('is difficulty rising?') accrues once difficulty is tagged at case-add time.

items.hypothesis: Difficulty is model-relative (2026-07-06: 4 of l0-ponytail's 7 hand tags were wrong for deepseek-chat — 'toy' debounce/deep-clone catch its baseline, 'realistic' fetch-user/ship-email pass unaided). So derive per-case tags from the MEASURED baseline majority verdict in runs/log.jsonl (1=baseline-pass/convergence-prone, 2=baseline-fail/discriminating; 3 stays hand-only), with a per-set difficultyBasis recording model+timestamp+N for traceability.
items.ship_test: All 7 sets tagged from measurement; dark-room reads 7/7 tagged, 0 dark rooms, 0 untagged; the known-wrong hand tags are corrected by data, not by opinion.
